facts.raw_span: A 76-year-old woman
history of appendicitis, torsion of an ovarian cyst pedicle, and uterine myoma
rapidly enlarging right parietal mass behind the ear over one month
no neurological deficits or systemic symptoms
laboratory studies, including complete blood counts, metabolic panel, and viral serology for HIV and Epstein-Barr virus, were all normal or negative
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a 5-cm hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed a heterogeneously enhancing lesion in the right parietal region
Cerebral angiography demonstrated a vascular tumor supplied by the middle meningeal artery
a clinical diagnosis of osteoblastic meningioma was made
intraoperatively, the tumor was extradural, caused skull destruction, and had no intradural involvement
Histology showed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm
positive immunostaining for α-smooth muscle actin, vimentin, and desmin, and negative staining for Epstein-Barr virus

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging parietal mass, hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion, and heterogeneously enhancing lesion on MRI, along with the intraoperative findings of an extradural tumor with skull destruction, are consistent with meningeal sarcomatosis.

The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging parietal mass, hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion, and heterogeneously enhancing lesion on MRI, along with the intraoperative findings of an extradural tumor with skull destruction, are consistent with osteosarcoma of the skull.
The patient's histology showing a malignant spindle cell neoplasm with positive immunostaining for α-smooth muscle actin, vimentin, and desmin is consistent with leiomyosarcoma.

The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging parietal mass, hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion, and heterogeneously enhancing lesion on MRI, along with the histology showing a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, are consistent with malignant fibrous histiocytoma.

The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging parietal mass, hyperdense meningeal mass with parietal bone invasion, and heterogeneously enhancing lesion on MRI, are consistent with solitary fibrous tumor.
